title: Oracle NVL Function
rule: Oracle NVL function can be migrated to Snowflake using the COALESCE function. Verify datatype compatibility when the arguments have different data types.

title: Oracle DECODE Function
rule: Oracle DECODE expressions should generally be converted to CASE expressions in Snowflake for better readability and ANSI SQL compatibility.

title: Oracle CONNECT BY
rule: Oracle hierarchical queries using CONNECT BY PRIOR should be redesigned using recursive common table expressions in Snowflake.

title: Oracle Autonomous Transactions
rule: Oracle autonomous transactions do not have a direct equivalent in Snowflake stored procedures and usually require application or process redesign.

title: Oracle Exception Handling
rule: Oracle PL SQL exception handling should be reviewed and converted to Snowflake Scripting exception handling where supported.

title: Oracle Sequences
rule: Oracle sequences can be migrated to Snowflake sequences using CREATE SEQUENCE. Verify increment values and usage patterns.

title: Oracle Temporary Tables
rule: Oracle global temporary tables should be evaluated carefully because temporary table behavior and session scope may differ in Snowflake.

title: Oracle Dynamic SQL
rule: Oracle dynamic SQL using EXECUTE IMMEDIATE can be migrated to Snowflake Scripting dynamic SQL, but identifier handling and parameter binding should be validated.

title: Oracle NUMBER Datatype
rule: Oracle NUMBER columns should be mapped to Snowflake NUMBER with appropriate precision and scale based on source data profiling.

title: Oracle MERGE Statement
rule: Oracle MERGE statements are generally supported in Snowflake, but source query behavior and duplicate matching conditions should be validated.
